stories.headline: Texans and Colts are each trying to avoid 0-3 starts in matchup between struggling AFC South teams
stories.summary: — Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen and Houston Texans coach DeMeco Ryans understand the urgency of Sunday's early season AFC South matchup.
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- — Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen and Houston Texans coach DeMeco Ryans understand the urgency of Sunday's early season AFC South matchup.


The winner could find themselves tied for the division lead. The loser will spend the rest of the season dealing with the ramifications from an 0-3 start.


It's just that simple, even if they would rather focus on the here and now.


“To start 0-2 is somewhere we don’t want to be," Ryans said Wednesday, two days after blaming himself for the two losses.


“Unfortunately, we’ve been here before, but to me, the past years of where we’ve been, it really doesn’t have any impact on where we are now.”


The Texans certainly know the history of such a dismal start.


Only seven teams in league history reached the playoffs after losing their first three games, only six did it over a full season and only one franchise has done it twice — Houston in 2018 and again last season when it needed a 12-2 finish to make its third straight postseason appearance.


This time seems different, though, given that the Texans already are 0-2 at home and managed just two field goals in last week's loss to Cincinnati.


Indy (0-2), meanwhile, hasn't gone 0-3 since 2021 when it rallied to a 9-8 mark — a season that started their current five-year playoff drought that put general manager Chris Ballard and Steichen, the third-year coach, squarely on the hot seat even before this season began.


But the Colts defense has struggled mightily so far, giving up a total of 74 points and more than 500 yards in each of its first two games.


Plus, the Colts have lost five straight to Houston — all by one score. So the stakes are high for Steichen and his team.


“Yeah, it’s a big matchup,” he said. “Any division games are a big matchup, especially Houston. I’ve got a lot of respect for them and what they do. But again, we've got to find ways to win these close games at the end because — especially division games — if you want to win the division, you’ve got to win division games.”


That quest begins Sunday.


Need to know
Houston (0-2) at Indianapolis (0-2).


When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, CBS.


Latest odds: Texans by 2 1/2.


Against the spread: Texans 0-2; Colts 1-1.


Last week: Texans lost to Bengals 20-6; Colts lost to the Chiefs 33-30 in OT.


Last meeting: Texans beat the Colts 38-30 on Jan. 4, 2026, in Houston.


Series record: Colts lead 33-15-1.


Matchup to watch
Texans ground game vs. Colts run defense: Indy's problems start in the front seven. Derrick Henry dominated them for 144 yards and three scores in Week 1. Last week, the Chiefs delivered a strong one-two combination with Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson teaming up for another 132 yards on the ground. Houston, meanwhile, has struggled mightily so far. The Texans two rushers, David Montgomery and Woody Marks have rushed are averaging a total of 60 yards per game and each are under 3.0 yards per carry. So whichever team gets the upper hand in this matchup may finally produce a winning hand.


Stats and stuff
— Houston QB C.J. Stroud had his fourth career 350-yard game last week, finishing with 353. He is 5-1 with eight TD passes and one TD run with one interception all time against Indy.


—- Last week, Dalton Schultz set Texans' single-game records for a TE by catching 12 passes for 140 yards. Both numbers were career highs and it marked the second time Schultz produced double-digit catches or a 100-yard game. Star WR Nico Collins missed the game with an injury.


— Houston DE Will Anderson tied a career high with eight tackles and had three tackles for loss and one sack last week. He had 12 TFLs in eight road games last season with at least one in each road game.


— The Texans have yet to force a turnover this season after having the third-most takeaways (29) in 2025.


— Indy has lost nine straight games going back to last season, the longest active streak in the league. The Colts also have lost four consecutive home games, a streak that began with a loss to Houston in November.


— The Colts will be without their top WR Alec Pierce, who went on injured reserve after injuring his left heel in last week's game. They have added veteran Darius Slayton, who could play after being reunited with QB Daniel Jones. Slayton and Jones were teammates with the Giants.


— Keenan Allen needs one catch to pass former Texans star Andre Johnson (1,062) for No. 12 on the league's career receptions list. He needs nine catches to pass Colts receivers coach Reggie Wayne (1,070) for 11th.


— RB Jonathan Taylor needs three total TDs to pass Wayne (82) for No. 3 in franchise history.


------


AP Sports Writer Kristie Rieken in Houston contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Former England forward Andy Carroll says he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021
stories.summary: Former England forward Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.
stories.body:
Former England forward Andy Carroll has said in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.

The 37-year-old included the details in his book, titled "Owning It." As a victim of sexual assault, Carroll was automatically granted anonymity.

Carroll said the incident took place at his home during a second spell at Newcastle. The offender -- a friend of his former partner, who was staying away at the time -- was later jailed for three years, with Carroll having testified in court.

Former Liverpool and West Ham striker Carroll, who is now a player/co-owner of National League South club Dagenham & Redbridge, said the incident happened when he was sleeping. He said he then threw the man out of the house, and knocked him unconscious when he attempted to get back inside.

"I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now," wrote Carroll, who had decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing it with his girlfriend, Lou Teasdale.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

"Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

Carroll said testifying in court, where the attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register, was "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous."

The 37-year-old said: "What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football ... The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

stories.headline: PWHL to host league's 1st All-Star Game next March in Toronto
stories.summary: The PWHL announced its first All-Star event will take place next year, marking another significant milestone for the league's continued growth and expansion.
stories.body:
The PWHL announced its first All-Star event will take place next year, marking another significant milestone for the league's continued growth and expansion.

PWHL All-Star -- set for March 7, 2027, in Toronto -- was revealed in a media release Thursday. The showcase will feature a four-team, 3-on-3 tournament at Scotiabank Arena with its own unique format.

The teams themselves -- made up of 10-player rosters with six forwards, three defenders and one goaltender -- will be made up of groups from PWHL Canada, PWHL International, PWHL USA, and PWHL Rookies. In this instance, all players in their first PWHL season, regardless of age, are eligible for the rookies' team.

After an opening round robin, there will be a semifinal game to determine who faces the top-ranked squad in the PWHL All-Star Final.

The All-Stars will be chosen through a combination of fan, player and media voting. Reserve players will be selected by league hockey operations.

The PWHL launched its inaugural regular season in 2024 with a matchup between Toronto and New York. The league has been working toward creating a signature event such as an All-Star Game to spotlight its established and rising stars.

"The PWHL was built to feature the best players in the world, and now fans will see the highest level of skill in women's hockey showcased in a new and unique way," said Jayna Hefford, PWHL executive vice president of hockey operations, in a statement. "The 3-on-3 format creates an intense, fast-paced style of play, while the mix of teams will produce intriguing matchups and give both established stars and emerging talent the opportunity to shine. It's only fitting that we return to Toronto -- where the PWHL first dropped the puck -- to bring the best of the best together for an unforgettable day for our fans and our league."

stories.headline: Lachie Neale ban overturned, free to play AFL Grand Final
stories.summary: Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL grand final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.
stories.body:
Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL Grand Final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.

The dual Brownlow Medal winner will feature in the premiership decider against Fremantle - his former club - at the MCG on Saturday after having a striking charge on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan downgraded on Thursday.

Neale will instead be fined $10,000.

He initially failed in challenging the one-game ban from the match review officer at the tribunal on Tuesday night.

To succeed on appeal, Brisbane had to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

The Lons were able to sway the appeals board that the tribunal had made an error of law in not considering the exceptional and compelling circumstances of Neale not having previously been suspended in 320 AFL games.

Neale avoids becoming the first player to miss an AFL grand final following a preliminary-final suspension since Collingwood's Anthony Rocca in 2003.

Brisbane legal representative Adrian Anderson tried various different arguments to clear Neale.

One included suggesting the ban should be served in round one next year, instead of in the grand final, due to the added importance of the match.

It was a bold strategy given Neale is almost certain to leave Brisbane and join Collingwood during the off-season.

Anderson leaned heavily on Neale's prior record of not being suspended, referring to the four-time All-Australian as "pretty close to a unicorn".

Introduced this year, the "exceptional and compelling circumstances" clause had been deployed once: to downgrade a one-game ban to Collingwood legend and AFL games record-holder Scott Pendlebury, to a fine.

New vision of Neale's strike on Ginnivan became available on Thursday, but was not allowed to be used because it was not shown at Tuesday's tribunal hearing.

The footage would have shown a clearer picture of the incident and likely not helped Neale's case.

Sydney's Barry Hall (2005) and Richmond's Trent Cotchin (2017) famously escaped bans for incidents in their respective preliminary finals to play in eventual premiership wins.

The Lions named Neale in their team on Thursday, shortly before the decision was handed down, and didn't need to change the 23.

With rain expected for Saturday's grand final, Neale will figure prominently as one of the Lions' best wet-weather players.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

stories.headline: Columbus Crew 2 fires Higuain after fallout from ref abuse
stories.summary: The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.
stories.body:
The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.

"We determined it's in the best interest of our Club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuaín from his responsibilities," said Crew General Manager Issa Tall in prepared statement. "After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our Club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met," The Crew's statement added that for the 2026 MLS NEXT Pro Playoffs, the Crew 2 technical staff will assume additional responsibilities ahead of the Club's search for a full-time head coach for the side.

Higuain, 41, was suspended for two games following an Aug. 23 incident that involved him refusing to let go of the hand of a female referee during the post-game handshake, despite being asked three times to do so. Higuain also directed a sexist remark toward the referee saying: "Don't forget that this is a man's game."

Higuain, who excelled as a player for the Crew over eight seasons, was red carded for the incident. In addition to the two-game suspension, Higuain was ordered to undergo restorative practice training, sources told ESPN.

An MLS NEXT Pro spokesperson confirmed that Higuain was suspended for just one additional game, as the policy allows for the red card to count towards the total suspension. The same spokesperson wasn't able to answer the question of why Higuain's actions didn't constitute a forceful grab.

The Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA), the union that represents MLS and USL referees, brought the incident to light over the weekend, stating in a social media post that it was not satisfied with the penalties, adding that a "forceful grab" plus the discriminatory language should have been penalized more severely.

While the PSRA's post didn't mention Higuain by name, ESPN reported that the coach in question was Higuain.

"The League's response falls drastically short of the right message to the participants, the referees, and the public. It needs to be reevaluated," the PSRA's social media post read.

The Crew initially issued a statement stating that, "The Crew actively collaborated with MLS NEXT Pro throughout the review process and fully accepted the additional discipline issued in accordance with league policies.

"We condemn any action or notion that contradicts our mission of uniting and uplifting all communities and genders through the global game."

But sources with knowledge of the Crew's decision to fire its coach told ESPN that the club wasn't satisfied with Higuain's response to the incident, saying there was a "lack of contrition" on his part, that he refused to issue a public apology to the female referee, and that there was an overall lack of accountability on the part of its second-team coach.

There was pressure from several of the Crew's supporters groups as well, including the Nordecke and CapyBrava, which both made social media posts demanding that Higuain be fired.

One source said that Higuain was informed of the club's decision early Tuesday afternoon.

In a statement given to ESPN on Sunday, MLS NEXT Pro said the league "immediately investigated the reported incident between the head coach and the female official. It was determined that the coach's behavior violated League policies and warranted additional discipline beyond the red card that was issued in the moment. He served a two-game suspension and is required to participate in a multi-session restorative practices process, which is already underway. The program is intended to support the League's efforts to foster understanding, accountability, respect, and the restoration of relationships across the League. MLS NEXT Pro believes in the restorative approach. The League is confident in its process and the results."

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Selwyn Cobbo named Queensland's best for State of Origin
stories.summary: Queensland winger Selwyn Cobbo justified his State of Origin recall by winning the Ron McAuliffe Medal at the QRL awards night.
stories.body:
Dolphins winger Selwyn Cobbo received a boost ahead of the NRL preliminary final after winning Queensland's best player award for the State of Origin series.

The 24-year-old scored four tries, made four line breaks and averaged a stunning 184m across the three matches of 2-1 series loss. He was recalled by coach Billy Slater after a two-year absence from the Origin arena, due to the stellar club form he has displayed for the Dolphins.

Cobbo was a worthy winner of the Ron McAuliffe Medal, named in honour of the former senator and influential boss of the Queensland Rugby League.

Cobbo will play against the Sydney Roosters in the grand final qualifier on Friday night.

He won the Queensland gong at the QRL season awards on Thursday night in Brisbane, 17 years after Maroons legend Greg Inglis, who was his idol growing up.

Maroons prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui took out the FOGS Peter Jackson Memorial Award after his brave and emotional display in game two in Melbourne, where he played his heart out just days after his father Fereti Fa'asuamaleaui had died.

The Maroons won the match 44-24.

The award, named in honour of late Queensland star Jackson, is presented to a Maroons player or one of the support staff who epitomises what the Queensland Origin spirit is all about

Cobbo moved to the Dolphins from Brisbane this year and has had a career-best season under head coach Kristian Woolf.

He took on board advice from Maroons coach Slater, who gave him his debut in 2022.

"I'd been there in Origin for a couple of years but didn't play last year, which wasn't the best year for me," Cobbo said.

"I wanted to get back, so I worked really hard the whole off-season. All the extras I was doing paid off.

"As Billy says, if you work hard for it the rewards will come. He was real good throughout the camps, the staff as well.

"Just knowing I can play 80 minutes of Origin was a shock to me, but I enjoyed every moment of it."

Cobbo recently re-signed with the Dolphins until the end of 2031 after finding his feet following a disappointing 2025 at the Broncos.

"The club has done a lot for me. They told me they would bring me back to Origin, and I just want to give back to them and play good footy here for the next five years," he said.

Cobbo's fierce ball running in Origin this year would have made Inglis proud.

"He was my idol growing up, the way he played ... strong. It would have been hard defending against him," Cobbo said.

Now Cobbo is on track to cap off a great season with a recall to the Australian side under his old club coach Kevin Walters at the World Cup, which is another goal.

"It would be good to chuck on that (Australian) jersey again and play under Kevvie. I'll work hard to get back there," he said.

stories.headline: Judge denies request to seal records in Josh Jacobs case
stories.summary: The judge who presided over the criminal case of Packers RB Josh Jacobs denied a request by the victim to have evidence permanently sealed.
stories.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The judge who presided over the criminal case of Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs denied a request by the victim to have evidence permanently sealed and instead turned the matter over to the police department that conducted the criminal investigation.

Brown County (Wisconsin) District Court judge Marc A. Hammer made the determination during a hearing Thursday. When his order goes into effect on Friday, it will cancel a temporary order to seal that he issued on Sept. 10.

However, it does not mean the records, which includes surveillance video outlined in the criminal report that states a portion of the incident was caught on camera, will be immediately released. Instead, the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department will handle any new requests made under public records laws.

ESPN and several media outlets previously filed requests for evidence in the case, and those requests must now be resubmitted once the seal is lifted.

If the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department decides to release the evidence, the victim or Jacobs will be entitled to appeal before anything is released.

A permanent sealing of evidence could have prevented the NFL from reviewing the video from the May 23 incident at Jacobs' home in Green Bay.

Jacobs was placed on the NFL's commissioner exempt list on Aug. 30 and cannot play or practice. He could be subject to a suspension once the NFL concludes its investigation. Time spent on the commissioner exempt list would count toward a suspension. Thursday's ruling, however, does not guarantee that the NFL will get the video, as it would have to file a request as well.

According to the criminal complaint, Jacobs threw the woman, identified as "ANM," to the ground and damaged her phone, and there is surveillance video of the portion of the incident that took place in Jacobs' garage.

Jacobs entered a no contest plea on Sept. 10. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgement agreement on a charge of damage to property. He was ordered to have no contact with the victim, pay restitution, attend counseling and be under supervision for one year. Both were misdemeanors charges.

stories.headline: Is Sullivan the next Olise? Comparisons for USMNT's top young stars
stories.summary: With the USMNT welcoming a new class of debutantes during this international break, ESPN dives into the numbers of the United States' next prodigies.
stories.body:
If one word defines the first call-up for the U.S. men's national team since the summer's FIFA World Cup, it's this: youth.

To give the next generation some opportunities, coach Mauricio Pochettino has given several key figures a break and instead selected a noticeably younger group for upcoming friendlies in late September and early October.

Of the 28 chosen, 13 have yet to make their senior national team debut. From those 13, eight are teenagers who are continuing to fine-tune and develop their talents.

Though some of these players are literally still kids, they also represent an exciting generation of up-and-comers who have the potential to become elite game changers for the U.S. by the time the 2030 World Cup rolls around, if not sooner.

Shining a light on a few of these fresh faces, we've selected five names to follow in the upcoming international break. We've also enlisted the help of ESPN's in-house guru Bill Connelly, who has provided key stats (over the last 365 days in all competitions) on each name, as well as both overly optimistic and realistic comparisons to players that they could one day become.

Zavier Gozo | Midfielder | 19 | Crystal Palace

Within just three years, Gozo went from earning his MLS debut in 2023 with Real Salt Lake to then gaining a high-profile move to the Premier League this summer with Crystal Palace.

Typically playing on the right flank, the 19-year-old midfielder has an immense amount of energy with 8.1 progressive carries per 90 minutes. In fact, even though Gozo hasn't played in MLS since July -- before his move to the Premier League -- he still ranks second overall in MLS for total progressive carries, carries following a defensive action, and take-ons, among teenagers in MLS.

"He is insanely robust. If I were to tell you the running numbers he's putting up, they're, for his age, I think world-class," said Nate Miller, a former assistant at Real Salt Lake, to ESPN.

With six goals and five assists across 1,614 minutes in the last year, the attack-minded midfielder has stepped up with his 3.1 shots per 90 minutes. He is also crucial in regaining the ball thanks to his 6.8 defensive interventions per 90 minutes. Looking back at teenagers within MLS, Gozo is still second in 2026 when it comes to total tackles.

"We don't know who's going to come through," said Miller about the next generation of U.S. stars. "But he should be one of the main guys in the national team in the future."

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Barcelona and Spain's Lamine Yamal

More realistic comparison: Leeds United's Brenden Aaronson

Mathis Albert | Midfielder | 17 | Borussia Dortmund

When Albert stepped onto the pitch in April for German side Borussia Dortmund, the midfielder made history as the youngest American to play in the Bundesliga at the age of 16. Since then, his appearances have been limited as a backup option on the bench --- which will skew some of our stats --- but the midfielder remains an intriguing option for the future of the national team.

Across all competitions, the former LA Galaxy academy player is averaging 8.3 progressive carries, 3.3 shots and 11.9 ground duels per 90 minutes.

"He was fearless, he was brave, he was relentless," said U.S. youth national team coach Gonzalo Segares to Goal.com about Albert.

"What stood out was his one-on-one ability. That's something we look at in players: being comfortable to take on players and beat them. That's a special talent that we look for in attacking players, and he had it."

When watching clips of the player, his pace, dribbling and tenacity (typically on the left wing) immediately shine. During his last appearance for Dortmund earlier this month, the South Carolina native led his team in shots, dribbles and ground duels in a 5-0 victory over HEBC Hamburg in the German Cup.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: PSG and Georgia's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia

More realistic comparison: Real Betis and Morocco's Abde Ezzalzouli

Cavan Sullivan | Midfielder | 16 | Philadelphia Union

There is no young American player gaining more hype or attention than the Manchester City-bound Sullivan. Set to join the Premier League giants when he turns 18, the attacking midfielder has kept pace with the likes of Lionel Messi since MLS returned to play after the World Cup.

The league leaders in goal contributions after the summer break? That's Sullivan and Messi with 13 apiece.

"A lot of attention goes on the creative things that he brings to the game," said interim head coach Ryan Richter to ESPN. "But the thing that stands out to me the most is his mentality and his competitiveness and the way that he approaches every single day."

In MLS, Sullivan is averaging 1.10 goals+assists, 2.4 chances and 2.9 shots per 90 minutes. More than just a dynamic chance-creator, improving finisher, and scrappy recoverer of the ball, there's an undeniable level of confidence in a player that makes clever on-the-field decisions that's far beyond his years. He is also incredibly fun to watch with his technical flair that's on display, as seen with this backheel goal this month.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Bayern Munich and France's Michael Olise

More realistic comparison: Arsenal and Greece's Christos Tzolis

Julian Hall | Forward | 18 | Red Bull New York

The highest-scoring teenager in MLS this season? That plaudit belongs to Red Bull New York forward Hall, who leads the 16-19 age group with a total of 10 goals across 26 appearances.

Efficiency comes to mind for the player who has 51% of his shots hitting the target, which ranks him seventh across MLS when analyzing those who have at least 10 goals this season.

Across all competitions, Hall has 18 goal contributions across 2,448 minutes in the past year, an average of 2.3 shots per 90 minutes, and is noticeably focused on close-range opportunities with 82.3% of shots emerging from inside the 18-yard box. In his first start of the 2026 season, the striker also gained plenty of attention after scoring twice for his club in a 2-1 victory.

"What stands out to me with Julian is his mentality," coach Michael Bradley said to ESPN.

"Obviously, the speed, the ability to change a game, the ability to get behind defenders and make things happen, those things are clear. He has a real belief in himself. He's willing to listen, he wants to learn, and he's constantly trying to understand how he can get better. You see that in the way he works every day."

Smart with his movement and runs, as well as a decent short passing game in the final third, expect him to be a possible difference-maker in the upcoming international window.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Atlético Madrid and Canada's Jonathan David

More realistic comparison: Borussia Dortmund and Portugal's Fábio Silva

Adri Mehmeti | Midfielder | 17 | Red Bull New York

While Hall is scoring goals, his teammate Mehmeti is doing plenty of the supporting work in the heart of the Red Bull starting XI.

With 6.6 ball recoveries per 90 minutes, the 17-year-old not only leads his team in recoveries but also the entire league in 2026. Thanks to his 77.9 touches and 9.0 line-breaking passes per 90 minutes, Mehmeti is also the league leader for touches and through balls among teenagers this season. Able to win the ball back and create opportunities going forward, Mehmeti impacts the defense and attack in any given match.

"For Adri, I think it's about continuing to develop the physical side and the defensive side of his game while maintaining the qualities that make him special with the ball," Bradley said to ESPN.

"He's playing a lot of minutes and taking on more responsibility, so now the challenge is learning how to manage a game for 90 minutes and understanding when to take risks, when to keep the ball, when to play forward and when to help the team breathe."

With friendlies against the likes of Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada coming up, we'll see if he can maintain that unfazed calm in his first call-up with the national team.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Manchester City and England's Elliot Anderson

More realistic comparison: Internazionale and England's Curtis Jones

stories.headline: WNBA playoff picture 2026: How will final seeds be set Thursday?
stories.summary: Before the playoffs open Sunday, the final four seeds will be set in Thursday's regular-season finales.
stories.body:
Four seeds are set for the 2026 WNBA playoffs, but the other four come down to Thursday, the last night of the regular season. Five games are on the schedule, and four have playoff implications.

The Minnesota Lynx are the No. 1 seed, secured Tuesday thanks to the Golden State Valkyries' loss at the Portland Fire.

The other seeds were set Wednesday after the Atlanta Dream's 83-65 win over the New York Liberty. That put the Dream into the No. 4 seed and the Liberty into No. 8, plus locked the Dallas Wings into No. 7.

Minnesota and New York will meet in the first round.

Here's how the remaining seeds and playoff matchups will be decided.

Nos. 2 and 3 seeds

Golden State and the defending champion Las Vegas Aces will host first-round games but are still jockeying for position.

On Thursday, the Valkyries (31-12) play at the Los Angeles Sparks, while the Aces (30-13) visit the Phoenix Mercury. Golden State will get the No. 2 seed with a victory or a Las Vegas loss.

But if Golden State loses and Las Vegas wins, both teams finish 31-13, and the Aces will be the No. 2 seed. They own the tiebreaker thanks to their 3-0 regular-season record against the Valkyries.

Nos. 5 and 6 seeds

This will come down to the Indiana Fever and the Washington Mystics.

Thursday, Indiana plays at Minnesota two days after the Fever's 96-77 win over the Lynx in Indianapolis on Tuesday. Lynx point guard Olivia Miles didn't play in that game because of a calf injury and has already been ruled out for Thursday.

With a victory, the Fever will get the No. 5 seed, as they will finish 29-15. However, if the Fever lose and Washington beats the Chicago Sky, the Fever and the Mystics would finish 28-16. In that case, Washington would be the No. 5 seed and Indiana No. 6 since the Mystics have the tiebreaker with their 2-1 regular-season series record against the Fever.

If the Fever end up at No. 6, that will be their third season in a row with that seed. The Mystics missed the playoffs the past two seasons.

Playoffs open Sunday

All four best-of-three first-round playoff series begin Sunday, starting on the home court of the higher seed. If the series goes to a deciding Game 3, the higher seed hosts that game, too.

"Little things matter in the playoffs, and that might be one of them," Atlanta's Naz Hillmon said Wednesday about the Dream being in the top four and having home-court advantage in the first round. "Just having that energy behind us from our fans."

stories.summary: Using an analytical lens, Dean Oliver examines what the NBA Rank panel got right -- and what it got very wrong.
stories.body:
When combing through ESPN's latest countdown of the top 100 NBA players, try to remember one phrase, which is just as applicable to ranking players as it is to building a winning roster.

People see the game better than numbers, but numbers see all the games.

As it relates to NBA Rank 2026, those numbers are a collective of advanced player ratings commonly in use, from ESPN's Net Points to DARKO, LEBRON, EPM and RAPM. Those systems can provide a useful counter perspective to the humans, with their good eyes but occasional biases.

With the full top 100 unveiled for the 2026-27 season, let's examine what the metrics revealed about which player rankings our panelists got right -- and which they got wrong.

Four things NBA Rank got wrong
1. Jalen Brunson (No. 6)

Our last view of Brunson is him carrying the Knicks to a fourth-quarter comeback in Game 5 of the NBA Finals. He was tremendous in New York's run to the championship -- but that leads to the bias that he will maintain it.

He was Finals MVP, but will he really finish the season as the league's sixth-best player? Brunson has always been limited a bit by his size (6-foot-2, 190 pounds) and his defense, something the metrics perhaps see and remember more than the seven panelists remember the late buckets he poured in to win the Finals. Those problems are likely to persist.

I love Brunson's game, but his lofty ranking benefitted not only from recent bias but also from the New York media bias. (That bias might also help you forget that Brunson missed the shot in the most iconic image from the Finals, when OG Anunoby swooped in for the putback game-winner to clinch Game 4.)

The metrics place Brunson around the No. 25 range heading into the season. That's not a huge gap. He's elite, just not No. 6 -- at least not during the regular season.

2. Rookies

Another bias comes from wanting to believe the hype. AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, Cameron Boozer and Caleb Wilson all make the top 100, but rookies are generally bad NBA players -- predraft highlights don't show the turnovers, or the missed boxouts, or the poor defense.

Is it possible one or two rookies end the year in the top 100 of Net Points per game, per 100 possessions, or another metric? Of course. It's a strong draft, but history suggests these rankings could be a year too early.

3. Jaylen Brown (No. 14)

Without the rehabbing Jayson Tatum, the Celtics were picked to win about 40 games last year, so their overperformance led to a Coach of the Year award for Joe Mazzulla and to a shower of praise for Brown.

The claims of Brown being the league's "best two-way player" came mostly after he had his best game of the year against the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, but few noticed Brown's next game, where he scored 14 points on 24 field goal attempts. Maybe we term this a "highlight bias" because our voters perhaps saw those highlights and loved him, ranking Brown between No. 9 and No. 23. The metrics' average, meanwhile, was around No. 60.

The quick reasons the metrics don't rate Brown as highly are that the Celtics played better without him, he turns the ball over a lot and he doesn't have great vision. The not-so-quick reasons filled plenty of podcast space over the summer.

4. Collin Murray-Boyles is outside the top 100 and the computers don't like it.

The metrics see the Toronto Raptors second-year forward as comparable to Atlanta Hawks All-Star Jalen Johnson (No. 22 in NBA Rank) in his production this coming year. Murray-Boyles isn't the passer that Johnson has become, but he is a good defender who just doesn't yet shoot a lot from the perimeter. He's on the glass and he actually averaged more assists per 48 minutes as a rookie than Johnson did in either of his first two years.

With the 2025 rookies he entered the league with -- such as Cooper Flagg, Dylan Harper and Kon Knueppel -- Murray-Boyles didn't get the same publicity and didn't get enough ranking votes. But the computers saw him.

Four things NBA Rank got right
1. The top

As the analytics revolution has played out, the general perception of good players has become more consistent with metrics. Coaches know better and don't just let bad shooters toss up shots to get inefficient points. Fans know better, too.

This year, the aforementioned Brown has a gap between metrics and the general perception, but much of the NBA Rank top 20 is spot on.

2. Paolo Banchero (No. 36)

For those who don't follow the NBA subtext on Banchero, you have missed frequent whispers about how much better Orlando is with him off the floor. But last year, those whispers might have become louder because the panel moved him down from No. 17 in 2025 to No. 36 this season.

Banchero had benefitted from the hype around top draft picks while he was still trying to build a jump shot and make his teammates better, but the gap between Banchero's perceived value and his on-court production is shrinking.

3. Ajay Mitchell (No. 79)

Mitchell was not a regular starter last year but was quite good on both sides of the floor. According to Genius IQ tracking, Mitchell was in the top 20 in points allowed per 100 matchups and shot quality allowed.

Across the spectrum of various metrics, he ranked in the top 30 leaguewide. That's far better than the No. 79 ranking our panelists gave, but that's the kind of variability that should get narrowed as Mitchell's responsibilities and exposure grow in Oklahoma City.

4. The impact of injuries

We aren't displaying the underlying variability in the voting on players, but players who were injured last season (such as Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton, Damian Lillard), who are still recovering (such as Jimmy Butler III), or who are chronically injured (such as Joel Embiid) have much more variability in how much they will contribute this year.

From an analytical perspective, one of the best predictors of future injury is past injury, and that leads to greater uncertainty about the quantity of playing time. Our voters captured that.

stories.headline: Jaspa Fletcher outlines Lachie Neale legacy ahead of crucial call
stories.summary: Jaspa Fletcher will line up for his fourth AFL grand final in as many seasons aware he may never run out alongside Lachie Neale again.
stories.body:
Jaspa Fletcher has spelt out the impact Lachie Neale has made at the club as he grapples with the prospect of never playing alongside him for the Brisbane Lions again.

The 22-year-old will contest a fourth AFL grand final in his fourth season when the Lions face Fremantle on Saturday at the MCG.

As it stands Neale won't join him, the star midfielder on Thursday set to appeal a one-match suspension for striking that has ruled him out of the club's tilt for a third-straight title.

Two-time Brownlow Medallist Neale is widely tipped to join Collingwood next season.

"That's footy and that's business, and he's got to do what's right for him," Fletcher said of the former captain's likely move.

"But I'd love to still have him here, because as a mate and as a mentor as well, I can't thank him enough for what he's done for me.

"He's left such a great legacy at the club. I'm sure we'll keep a great connection over the journey."

Neale rates Fletcher, endorsing him among a host of capable young Lions leaders as a potential future captain.

"When I heard that, I was super honoured," Fletcher said.

"If that's the way the club wants to go, I'd be more than happy to do it.

"I'd do anything for the club."

Fletcher hasn't missed a game since his 2023 debut but admits his form, after preseason shoulder surgery, hadn't met his own expectations.

"I've been pretty honest ... I haven't been overly proud with how I've gone about it," he said.

"I could have got a little bit more out of myself, but that's behind me now and I've learnt a lot of lessons along the road, on and off the field."

And, after losing the only junior football grand final he reached "by 100 points", he hasn't taken his AFL career for granted.

"I'm just a product of being part of such a great club as such a great time," he said.

"In '23 we couldn't get it done, so to win a couple now is awesome. In 2023 you learn about how to go about the day, the week.

"As much as you want to win that, it set us up."

stories.headline: Arman Tsarukyan elevates his position in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Walker's on but Woolf 'wouldn't swap' his own No.7
stories.summary: Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has shown the skill and mindset to win big games and coach Kristian Woolf backs him to the hilt for their preliminary final.
stories.body:
All the hype has been around the early return of Sydney Roosters halfback Sam Walker from injury but Dolphins coach Kristian Woolf has full faith his own No.7 has the skillset to shine in his biggest test yet.

Dolphins co-captain Isaiya Katoa, 22, will be integral to a win in the grand final qualifier against the Roosters at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night.

Katoa has 18 try assists this year in 21 games. Walker has 21 in the same number of matches.

In linebreak involvements Katoa is second best in the NRL behind only Cody Walker, boasting 31 this year. Sam Walker has nine for the season.

It is Katoa's cool, calm and collected ability to make others around him better with subtle touches that sets him apart and makes him such a danger to the opposition and a weapon for his team.

Woolf said he expected Walker, back from a four-week layoff with an ankle injury, to line up for the Roosters and bring "a bit of the unknown" to the game but is just glad the Dolphins have Katoa.

"I certainly wouldn't swap Isaiya for anyone," Woolf said.

"I love what he brings as a person and how he carries himself and he plays with that same calmness and confidence that he has got in himself.

"I am looking forward to what he can do tomorrow night."

Katoa played with maturity in his first final experience, the 26-16 win in the away qualifying final against the Warriors after the Dolphins trailed 16-8.

"What impressed me was that he kept his cool regardless of the score and a hostile crowd that did influence some decisions," Woolf said.

"It really impressed me how he turned the game in the second half with kicking. It was a 10 out of 10 (performance) and allowed us to put the Warriors under pressure."

Woolf's message to all his players has been to "enjoy the week" and back the toughness and skill that has got them this far.

Founding Dolphins forwards Jesse and Kenny Bromwich and Mark Nicholls spoke to the group on Thursday before their captain's run.

Woolf said the retired trio had "set a tone for what we want our culture to be and what sort of men we want representing the club".

"It was important for them to come in and brush shoulders with the players ... and the players loved seeing them," Woolf said.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson has big game experience with three NRL titles to his credit.

Woolf, however, knows about finals footy better than most after taking St Helens to three Super League titles and a Challenge Cup final victory.

Dolphins lock Morgan Knowles played in those wins under Woolf at St Helens.

"He's pretty consistent with his messages but once he gets to this time of the year, less is more," Knowles told AAP.

"I remember the grand final in 2020 against Wigan back in the UK he only showed us one video clip all week.

"It was when we previously played them in the year and they had a bit of a carry-on and were trying to impose themselves on us. That is all he needed to show."

The players were fired up enough to not leave anything in the tank.

"In the big games it comes down to the little moments when you are willing to keep turning up, put your body on the line and make the plays that don't get noticed," Knowles said.

The Dolphins beat the Roosters 26-12 in round 26 when Woolf's men defended their line with grit.

It was the template for a style the coach said had been a strength ever since they were flogged 66-0 by Cronulla in round 19. Since then the Dolphins have won eight straight and averaged 16.75 points against per match.
